summary: U.S. equities closed sharply lower on Friday as semiconductor stocks entered a bear market, dragging major indices to weekly losses. The S&P 500 fell 1.01% to 7,457.69, the Nasdaq dropped 1.4% to 25,520.24, and the Dow declined 0.77% to 52,146.42. The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell over 20% from its recent peak after Chinese startup Moonshot unveiled an advanced AI model that rivals U.S. competitors, rattling investor confidence in elevated tech valuations. Geopolitical tensions escalated as the U.S. launched a seventh consecutive night of airstrikes against Iran, sending oil prices higher while pressuring risk assets including crypto. Bitcoin retreated below $64,000 and Ethereum slipped under $1,900 as the Iran conflict dampened risk appetite. The Fed held rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% at its June meeting, with new Chair Kevin Warsh signaling a cautious stance amid elevated inflation driven partly by energy supply shocks. Meta shares fell despite reports of potential $10 billion cloud computing deal talks with Anthropic.

signals.title: Semiconductor selloff intensifies as Chinese AI breakthrough shakes valuations
signals.desc: The PHLX Semiconductor Index entered a bear market, falling 20% from its record as Moonshot's Kimi K3 AI model topped coding benchmarks, threatening U.S. chip dominance and pressuring Nvidia, AMD, and other semiconductor stocks.

signals.title: U.S.-Iran conflict escalates with seventh consecutive night of strikes
signals.desc: U.S. Central Command struck Iranian military targets for the seventh straight night, closing the Strait of Hormuz and sending oil prices surging while weighing on risk assets across equities and crypto markets.

signals.title: Crypto retreats as Bitcoin falls below $64K on geopolitical tensions
signals.desc: Bitcoin dropped to $63,130 and Ethereum fell to $1,832 as escalating Middle East conflict and renewed U.S.-Iran strikes dampened appetite for risk-based digital assets despite earlier gains from softer June inflation data.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh holds rates at 3.5%-3.75% citing elevated inflation
signals.desc: In his first FOMC meeting as Chair, Kevin Warsh kept the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.5%-3.75%, noting inflation remains elevated partly due to energy supply shocks from the Iran conflict, with June SEP showing potential for one rate hike before year-end.

signals.title: Meta falls 3.5% despite reports of $10B Anthropic cloud computing deal talks
signals.desc: Meta shares declined over 3% despite New York Times reports that Anthropic proposed a cloud computing rental deal worth up to $10 billion in June, though talks remain in early stages and may not materialize.

verdict: Risk-off sentiment dominates as semiconductor bear market and Iran conflict escalate, pressuring equities and crypto while oil surges on supply concerns.
